svg.title: Inkora AI architecture explained
svg.desc: A layered architecture diagram showing the user interface, orchestration, research and AI model adapters, database and authentication, and export and WordPress delivery, with numbered end-to-end flow.
svg.text: Inkora AI — how the system works
A layered writing pipeline: each part has a clear job, and providers can be replaced independently.
EXPERIENCE LAYER — the writing desk
Next.js · React · TypeScript · responsive workspace
Collects the brief · shows research sources · edits the outline/article · displays SEO review
User-facing screens only — vendor API keys and private secrets never belong in browser code.
brief + user actions
APPLICATION ORCHESTRATION — the coordinator
Validates input · checks permissions and rate limits · tracks workflow state
Chooses when to research, call a model, save progress or prepare an export
Handles provider errors, retries, timeouts and job coordination on the server.
search request
generation request
RESEARCH ADAPTERS
Connect to supported search services
Gemini Search grounding · Tavily
Normalize results into consistent source records:
title · URL · publisher · available metadata
MODEL ADAPTERS
Call a configured AI model through one interface
Gemini · OpenRouter · Groq
Draft sections · rewrite · summarize · structure output
Nara Router only after its API contract is verified.
reviewed source context + generated content
DATA & AUTHENTICATION
Supabase · PostgreSQL · user accounts
Projects · drafts · source records · settings · access control
Each user should only access their own authorized data.
DELIVERY & PUBLISHING
Export: Markdown · HTML · DOCX
WordPress REST API: create a draft
Ask for explicit confirmation before publishing live.
END-TO-END FLOW
Brief → validate → research → review sources & outline → draft → edit & SEO check → export / CMS draft
Human review stays in control. Search results and AI output must be checked before publication.
Conceptual target architecture — boxes describe planned responsibilities, not proof that every integration is already implemented.
